title: Granada
subtitle: The Last Kingdom of al-Andalus
simulation_note: This is a game, not a history. The valley, its steward, its crops, prices and seasons are invented for play. The places named are real, and what the museum knows of them is one link away. Historical review pending: the museum records linked here have not yet been through historical review for this game.

q02-harvest_text: Bring in the wheat of the mill field, or sell it: nine parts in ten at least.
q03-reserve_text: As winter approaches, hold twenty days of food for ten days running.

brief_text: Late spring. You are the steward of a valley district: sixty households, a store nearly full, and ninety-six days until the end of winter. The wheat of the mill field stands ripe. The olive terrace is thirsty behind a broken branch. The river meadow has never been watered.
outcome_won: The valley is fed, housed and watered.
outcome_lost: The winter ends with work undone.
reason_reserve: Less than {n} days of food in store
help_text: Let the days pass, or step them one at a time. Choose a tab to see the fields, the works and the market, and order what you decide. The top bar shows the valley now; the line under it shows what tomorrow and the next ten days will bring if you do nothing more. Every figure can be reached with the keyboard.

decision_water-for-the-neighbours_text: Their channel is running low in the heat. They ask for part of the river's flow for a while, and offer to pay for it. That village, its request and its offer are invented for the game.

brief_merchants-of-malaga: The first day of spring, a year on. The valley is fed; now it is asked to trade. The port offers two contracts, for olive oil and for vegetables: taking both pays more and leaves less to eat. You are asked to bring in dinars by trade, keep at least one contract, house more households, build a cistern against the dry weeks, and still hold the winter's food. The valley is as you left it. The port, its contracts and every figure are invented for the game.

help_ahead: The Overview lists what will go wrong if nothing more is done. It is the game's own rules run forward, and it changes when you act.
help_build: To build, open Construction, choose a building, then choose its ground. A ring shows where it would stand, and the game says why ground is refused.
help_trade: In the Economy, prices move overnight with what a market holds. The card "From the grove to the port" follows the olive oil step by step.
help_choose: In the 3D valley, click a field or a building to open its card. Photo mode puts the page away to take a picture; the game stands still meanwhile.
help_years: A year that is won can be followed by the next, with the valley as you left it: its people, its store, its buildings and what is sown.
help_keys: Keys: 1 to 5 open the five parts; P pauses; N passes a day; H opens this help; Escape leaves photo mode or stops the choosing of ground.

brief_a-dry-year: The first day of spring, in the third year. Little snow lies on the mountain: the river will run at about three quarters of a usual year, and less rain will fall. You are asked to hold two cisterns, to keep the households faring well for sixty days together, to go on trading, to keep the port's contract and to hold the winter's food. The village downstream will ask for water again. The valley is as you left it. This year, its river and every figure are invented for the game.
